name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gil Cisneros holds a roughly 9-to-1 fundraising edge in a D+8 district
Prediction markets price Cisneros around 95 percent to win
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so fundamentals carry the forecast
Challenger Eric Ching's modest warchest limits his ability to compete
model.rationale: Cisneros's incumbency, dominant fundraising, and the district's eight-point Democratic lean all point to a comfortable win, and markets agree at roughly 95 percent. With no polling or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, this remains a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Ching or new polling showing a much tighter race would be the main signals that could change this.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 31st District, centered in San Bernardino County, leans Democratic by about eight points. Incumbent Gil Cisneros is seeking re-election against Republican Eric Ching, a local city councilman. Cisneros has raised roughly $705,000 to Ching's $82,000 and holds a wide cash-on-hand advantage, with only minimal outside spending on either side. No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets price Cisneros's chances at about 95 percent.

The fundamentals line up behind the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, the value of incumbency, and a dominant fundraising position all point the same way. Ching would likely need a large infusion of outside money or a sharp shift in the political climate to make the race competitive, and neither is in evidence. The seat ranks among the safer Democratic holds on this year's House map.
